questions.question: Which statement best describes high-quality prenatal care?
choices: A fixed list of tests that is identical for every pregnancy
A longitudinal system of risk assessment, prevention, screening, education, symptom surveillance, and coordinated follow-up tailored to the patient
Only fetal heart-tone assessment after the first visit
Care that can ignore mental health and social barriers when vital signs are normal
questions.explanation: Prenatal care is ongoing and individualized. Medical, obstetric, mental-health, social, and access needs may change the monitoring and coordination plan over time.

questions.question: Which result is the best example of a prenatal screening result rather than a diagnosis?
choices: A positive cell-free DNA result indicating increased risk for a common fetal aneuploidy
A diagnostic result from a completed confirmatory procedure interpreted by the appropriate specialist
A confirmed blood type from a laboratory test
A measured maternal blood pressure
questions.explanation: Cell-free DNA is a screening test. A positive result increases risk but does not establish a diagnosis and should lead to counseling and an appropriate diagnostic follow-up pathway.

questions.question: What is the appropriate general approach to prenatal genetic screening and diagnostic testing discussions?
choices: Offer them only to patients older than 35 years
Discuss and offer screening and diagnostic options to all pregnant patients, while respecting the right to accept or decline
Order multiple overlapping screening tests simultaneously for every patient
Assume a negative screen eliminates all genetic and structural risk
questions.explanation: ACOG recommends discussing and offering prenatal genetic screening and diagnostic testing options to all pregnant patients regardless of age or baseline chromosomal-risk estimate.

questions.question: A patient has a positive cell-free DNA screen. What is the safest next step?
choices: Explain that the fetus definitely has the condition
Make an irreversible management decision from the screen alone
Explain that it is a screen, provide support, and coordinate genetic counseling and an appropriate diagnostic-testing pathway
Ignore the result because cell-free DNA has no clinical value
questions.explanation: Cell-free DNA is highly sensitive for common aneuploidies but is not diagnostic. A positive result requires careful counseling and an opportunity for confirmatory diagnostic testing.

questions.question: Which patient most clearly needs a tailored prenatal plan and likely expedited obstetric or maternal-fetal medicine collaboration?
choices: A patient with significant chronic kidney disease and chronic hypertension
A stable patient requesting a printed prenatal-visit schedule
A patient without symptoms who asks about oral health
A patient who wants to know the clinic’s phone number
questions.explanation: Significant kidney disease and chronic hypertension can materially change pregnancy risk, medication planning, and monitoring needs, warranting coordinated obstetric and specialty care.

questions.question: Which prenatal finding should prompt urgent obstetric or emergency evaluation rather than routine education alone?
choices: Persistent severe headache with visual changes, upper abdominal pain, and shortness of breath
A question about prenatal vitamins
Interest in a childbirth education class
A preference for telehealth scheduling when clinically appropriate
questions.explanation: Severe headache, visual changes, upper abdominal pain, dyspnea, and other warning signs can indicate serious maternal complications and need urgent assessment.

questions.question: What is the best interpretation of the term high-risk pregnancy?
choices: It is a stigmatizing label that should never be used
It means the patient has already developed a complication
It identifies a need for closer assessment, monitoring, or specialty support; risk exists on a spectrum and should not be used to shame the patient
It means primary care can no longer contribute to the patient’s care
questions.explanation: High-risk pregnancy describes a need for tailored care, not a moral judgment or final diagnosis. The FNP remains important for coordination, prevention, communication, and longitudinal support.

questions.question: Which vaccination statement is correct according to current CDC pregnancy guidance?
choices: Influenza vaccination and Tdap are recommended during every pregnancy; vaccine needs should be individualized by risk and current guidance
All vaccines are contraindicated during pregnancy
Live vaccines such as MMR should be given routinely during pregnancy
Vaccination history is irrelevant once a patient is pregnant
questions.explanation: CDC recommends influenza vaccination and Tdap during every pregnancy. Some live vaccines, including MMR and varicella, are not given during pregnancy, so current guidance and timing must be verified.

questions.question: What is the best way to implement perinatal depression and anxiety screening?
choices: Screen once at intake with no plan for results
Use validated screening at the initial prenatal visit, later in pregnancy, and postpartum, with systems for timely assessment, treatment, monitoring, and follow-up
Avoid screening if the patient appears calm
Screen only after a patient asks for psychiatric medication
questions.explanation: Screening needs a response pathway. ACOG supports validated perinatal depression and anxiety screening at initial prenatal, later pregnancy, and postpartum contacts with access to appropriate care.

questions.question: Which action best demonstrates closed-loop prenatal follow-up after an abnormal screening result?
choices: Assume another clinician will see the result
Tell the patient to search online for meaning
Document who reviews the result, explain what it does and does not mean, arrange the next evaluation, and confirm how the patient will be contacted
Wait until the next routine visit regardless of the result
questions.explanation: Closed-loop care assigns ownership, communicates meaning clearly, establishes the next step, and prevents abnormal results or referrals from being lost to follow-up.
